descripcion: Ruta A (desde A2) · Semana 1 · Introductions & everyday life

elementos.objetivo: Introduce yourself naturally, mixing permanent facts and things happening these days.
elementos.explicacion: Use the **present simple** for permanent facts and habits (*I study medicine. I live in…*). Use the **present continuous** for things happening now or around now (*I'm doing a rotation in pediatrics this month. I'm reading a great book these days.*). Natives mix both all the time when they introduce themselves. Useful time markers: **currently, these days, this month, at the moment**.
elementos.resumenES: Presente simple = hechos permanentes y hábitos. Presente continuo (am/is/are + -ing) = lo que pasa ahora o en esta temporada («these days», «this month»).

elementos.tituloES: Charla casual que no se corta
elementos.objetivo: Keep a conversation alive with follow-up questions and reactions.
elementos.explicacion: Conversations die when you answer and stop. Native speakers **react** (*Oh really? That sounds fun! No way!*) and **ask a follow-up question** (*How long have you…? What's it like?*). Remember question word order: **question word + do/does + subject + verb** (*Where do you work? What does she do?*).
elementos.resumenES: Para que la conversación no muera: reacciona + haz una pregunta de seguimiento. Orden de preguntas: Where/What + do/does + persona + verbo.

elementos.titulo: What did you do last weekend?
elementos.objetivo: Tell a short story about the past with common irregular verbs.
elementos.explicacion: Use the **past simple** for finished actions: *I went, I saw, I had, I met, I felt*. In questions and negatives, use **did + base verb**: *Did you go…? I didn't see…* (NOT *did you went*). To tell a story, connect ideas with **first, then, after that, in the end**.
elementos.resumenES: Pasado simple para acciones terminadas. En preguntas y negativas: did/didn't + verbo en forma base (nunca «did you went»). Conectores: first, then, after that, in the end.

elementos.objetivo: Describe your routine at the hospital using frequency adverbs.
elementos.explicacion: Frequency adverbs go **before the main verb** but **after to be**: *I **usually** start at 7.* / *I'm **always** tired after a shift.* Scale: always → usually → often → sometimes → hardly ever → never. Useful hospital vocabulary: **shift, on call, ward, rounds, check on patients**.
elementos.resumenES: Los adverbios de frecuencia van antes del verbo principal, pero después de «to be»: I usually start… / I'm always tired.

elementos.tituloES: Cierre de la semana 1: tu presentación de 2 minutos
elementos.objetivo: Combine everything from this week into a fluent 2-minute introduction.
elementos.explicacion: A strong self-introduction has a simple structure: **who you are** (present simple) → **what's happening in your life now** (present continuous) → **a recent story** (past simple) → **a question back** to keep it going. Don't aim for perfect grammar — aim for **no long pauses**. Fillers like *well…, you know…, I mean…* buy you time naturally.
elementos.resumenES: Estructura: quién eres (presente simple) → qué estás haciendo ahora (continuo) → una anécdota reciente (pasado) → una pregunta de vuelta. Prioriza la fluidez, usa muletillas como «well…», «you know…».

ejemplos.en: Well, I'm Sebastián. I'm a med student and I live with my family.
ejemplos.es: Bueno, soy Sebastián. Soy estudiante de medicina y vivo con mi familia.

ejemplos.en: These days I'm doing a rotation, so I'm pretty busy.
ejemplos.es: Estos días estoy rotando, así que ando bastante ocupado.

ejemplos.en: Last weekend, you know, I finally had a day off and went to the beach.
ejemplos.es: El fin de semana pasado, ya sabes, por fin tuve un día libre y fui a la playa.
